% 03.11.2025 CRL.M.(BAIL) 436/2023 (suspension of sentence)
1. The present application has been filed seeking suspension of sentence during the pendency of the appeal.
2. By way of the present appeal, the appellant seeks to assail the judgement of conviction dated 08.09.2022 and order on sentence dated 19.10.2022 vide which he has been directed to undergo RI for a period of 5 years for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(j)511 IPC with fine of Rs.5,000/- and in default thereof, to undergo SI for a period of six months.
The benefit of Section 428 Cr.P.C. has also been provided to the appellant, and all the sentences have been directed to run concurrently.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant/applicant submits that although the charge was framed under Section 376 IPC, the learned Trial Court convicted the appellant for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(j)/511 IPC and This is a digitally signed order.

He further submits that the impugned judgment was assailed on the ground that the testimony of the child victim was not recorded and that the forensic examination did not support the prosecution's case.

It is contended that while the victim's mother stated her Rinku vs State (Nct) Of Delhi And Anr on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88399290/
1 statement was recorded by PW-12, on the other hand, PW-10 claimed to have recorded the same,
thereby creating doubt regarding the investigation.

Reliance is also placed on the decisions in Saudan Singh vs. The State of Uttar Pradesh reported as 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3259 and Sonadhar vs. The State of Chhattisgarh reported as 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3182.
4.

5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

The contentions raised warrant detailed consideration; however, for the present, it is noted that the nominal roll dated 30.10.2025 of the appellant indicates that, as on that date, the unexpired period of his sentence is one year and one month.

6. Keeping in view the import of decisions and the fact that the hearing of the appeal will take some time, the sentence of the appellant/applicant is suspended during the pendency of the appeal on his furnishing of a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 10,000/- with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Trial Court/ Duty J.M./ link J.M./Jail Superintendent and also subject to the further following conditions:-
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 03/11/2025 at 23:41:28 (i) In case of change of residential address, the appellant shall promptly inform the same to the concerned Investigating Officer as well as to this Court.
(ii) The appellant shall regularly appear before the Court as and when the appeal is taken up for hearing.
(iii) The appellant will not get in touch directly or indirectly with the victim.
(iv) The appellant shall also provider his contact number to the IO and shall remain available on that number.
7. With the above directions, the application is disposed of.
8. A copy of this order be communicated electronically forthwith to the concerned Jail Superintendent for information and necessary compliance.
